transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because this has been going on for months now, and I don’t think I can just keep pretending it’s all coincidence. It’s a pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved around, and then no one tells me until after the fact, or they act like they “forgot” to call me back. Bills show up wrong, or with information missing, and when I ask about it, everyone has some excuse like it’s just a clerical error or a misunderstanding.

But it keeps happening. Over and over. And when something keeps happening that many times, I don’t see how I’m supposed to believe it’s all innocent mistakes. It feels like people are keeping information from me, like they’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of. And then when I point it out, they make it sound like I’m overreacting, but I’m not. I pay attention. I notice details. That’s been part of my work for years, so I know when things don’t add up.

Can you tell me more about how you feel people are keeping information from you? For example, do you feel this is happening randomly, or do you believe it’s being done on purpose to exclude or harm you?

No, I don’t think it’s random. That’s the thing. If it happened once or twice, fine, I could accept that—people make mistakes, offices are disorganized, bills get processed wrong sometimes. I’ve worked in office administration long enough to know mistakes happen. But when it’s the same kind of thing over and over, for months, and it always somehow leaves me out or puts me in the position of finding out after decisions are already made, then I don’t think that’s innocent.

Like with my sister’s appointments—suddenly the time changes, or someone says they left a message but I never got it, or I only hear about it after the fact. And then the bills come with wrong details or missing information, and when I call, they act confused or say it must have been a clerical issue. It’s always “miscommunication” or “someone forgot.” But it benefits the same people every time, because I’m the one who ends up not knowing what’s going on.

So yes, I do believe it’s being done on purpose. Maybe not everyone involved knows the whole thing, but enough people are keeping information from me. They’re trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of, and then when I question it, they make me sound unreasonable. That’s what bothers me most—being treated like I’m imagining a pattern that is clearly there.
Can you tell me if you have any idea who might be behind these actions, or if you’ve noticed any specific people involved in keeping information from you?

I can’t say it’s one single person with a name written at the top of it, if that’s what you mean. It’s more like… certain people keep ending up in the middle of it, and every time I try to pin down exactly who made the decision or who failed to call, suddenly no one knows, or it was “the system,” or “someone must have forgotten.” That’s part of what makes it so frustrating.

With my sister’s appointments, it’s the people handling the scheduling, and sometimes the people who are supposed to pass information along. The appointment gets moved, or I don’t hear about something until after it’s already happened, and then when I ask, they act like I’m making a big deal out of nothing. But it keeps happening in a way that leaves me out.

And then with the bills, same thing—wrong information, missing details, explanations that don’t really explain anything. I know how offices work. I supervised office staff for years. Mistakes happen, yes, but patterns happen too, and this is a pattern. So I don’t know if everyone involved knows exactly what they’re doing, but I do believe certain people are keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions I should be part of.
Do you ever feel like there’s a hidden meaning or purpose behind these events that others don’t seem to notice, something that feels very real to you even if other people don’t see it that way?

Yes… yes, I do. I mean, I wouldn’t say it in some strange way, like there’s a code in everything or anything like that, but there is a purpose behind it. That’s exactly what I’m trying to explain. Other people look at each thing by itself and say, “Oh, the appointment got moved, that happens,” or “The bill was wrong, that’s just a clerical error,” or “Someone forgot to call you back.” But they don’t look at the whole picture.

For months now, it’s been the same pattern. My sister’s appointments get changed and I’m not told until later, or I’m told someone called me when they didn’t. Bills come in with wrong information or missing pieces, and then when I ask questions, everyone has an excuse ready. And somehow the result is always that I’m left out, or I’m made to look like I’m being difficult for asking why it happened.

So yes, it feels very real to me that the purpose is to keep information from me and push me out of decisions I should be part of. Other people may not want to notice it, or maybe they think it’s easier to call it mistakes, but I know what a pattern looks like. I’ve dealt with paperwork and office systems for years. Things don’t just keep lining up the same way for no reason.
Have you ever felt that there’s a hidden plan or conspiracy against you, something that you can sense or understand but others don’t seem to recognize?

Yes, I suppose if you use the word “plan,” then yes… that’s what it feels like to me. I don’t know if I’d call it a conspiracy in the dramatic sense people mean, like some big movie thing, but there is something coordinated about it. Or at least intentional. It doesn’t feel accidental anymore.

I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved and somehow I’m not told until after, or someone claims they called me and I know I didn’t get a call. Then bills show up with wrong details or missing information, and when I ask questions, people “forget” to call me back or act like it’s just a mistake. One mistake, fine. Two mistakes, maybe. But over and over, and it always ends up with me being left out of decisions I should be part of? I can’t just ignore that.

Other people don’t seem to recognize it, or they don’t want to. They look at each incident separately, like, “Oh, these things happen.” But I’m looking at the whole chain of it. And from where I’m standing, it feels very clear that information is being kept from me and that I’m being pushed out. That’s what I keep trying to explain.
Have you ever felt that certain people or groups are deliberately working against you or trying to harm you in some way?

Yes. I mean… I don’t think they’re trying to physically hurt me, if that’s what you mean by harm, but working against me? Yes, absolutely. That’s why I’m here, because this has been going on for months now, and people keep acting like I’m supposed to just accept it as a string of innocent mistakes.

It’s the same pattern over and over. My sister’s appointments get moved, and somehow I’m not told until after the fact, or I’m told, “Oh, we called,” when I know I didn’t get a call. Then the bills come in wrong, or with pieces missing, or with information that doesn’t line up, and when I try to ask reasonable questions, suddenly people forget to call me back or they talk to me like I’m being unreasonable.

And I’ve worked in offices. I know things can fall through the cracks sometimes. But this isn’t one misplaced message or one bad bill. It keeps happening, and the end result is always the same: I’m left out, I’m made to look difficult, and decisions are happening without me having the information I should have. So yes, I do believe certain people are deliberately keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions. Other people may call it mistakes, but I know a pattern when I see one.
Have you ever felt that things people say or do, which seem unrelated to you, are actually directed at you or have a special meaning for you?

Yes… though I wouldn’t put it exactly like everything strangers say is about me. It’s more that when people say certain things, or when certain things happen, they’re not as unrelated as everyone wants me to believe.

Like with my sister’s appointments—one person says, “Oh, the schedule changed,” another says, “We left a message,” and then later someone else acts surprised that I didn’t know. On the surface those are separate little comments, right? But to me they fit together. They have a meaning. They’re telling me, in a roundabout way, that I’m not supposed to be included, or that they want me to feel like I’m the one who missed something.

And the bills are the same. A bill comes in wrong, or missing information, and then when I call, someone says, “That department handles it,” or “We’ll have someone call you back,” and then nobody does. People hear that and say it’s just office confusion. But I worked in offices for years. I know what normal confusion looks like. This is different because it keeps pointing in the same direction.

So yes, I do feel that some of what people say or do has a meaning for me that other people don’t seem to see. Not like secret messages on the television or anything like that, but in the way these so-called unrelated mistakes all keep adding up to me being kept out of decisions and not given the information I should have. Everyone else calls it coincidence. I don’t think it is.
Have you ever felt that events or actions by others, which seem unrelated to them, were specifically targeted at you or meant to send you a message that only you understand?

Yes, I have felt that. Not in a strange way like, you know, a coded message in the newspaper or something like that. It’s more practical than that, but it still feels very pointed.

I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved, and somehow I’m not told until after. Or someone says they called me, and I know I didn’t get a call. Then the bills show up wrong, or there’s missing information, or the details don’t match what I was told before. And when I call to sort it out, people suddenly “forget” to call me back, or they pass me around, or they act like I’m making too much of it.

If it happened once, I would let it go. I’ve worked in offices, I know mistakes happen. But when the same kind of mistake keeps happening and it always ends with me being left out or made to look like I’m the difficult one, then yes, it feels targeted. It feels like they’re sending the message that I’m not supposed to be involved, that I should just step aside and stop asking questions.

Other people keep telling me it’s just confusion or paperwork problems, but I don’t think so. I know what repeated mistakes look like, and I know when information is being kept from me. It’s the way everything adds up that people don’t seem to understand.

No, not really with the media or strangers. I’m not sitting at home thinking the television is talking to me, or that some person in a store is sending me a secret message. That’s not what this is.

What I’m talking about is much more specific, and honestly that’s part of why it frustrates me when people try to make it sound like I’m imagining things. I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s situation. Her appointments get moved and somehow I’m not told, or I’m told afterward, or someone says they called when I know I didn’t get the call. Then bills show up wrong, or incomplete, or with information that doesn’t match what I was told. And then when I call to ask about it, people “forget” to call me back, or I get passed from one person to another until nobody is responsible.

So no, it’s not messages in the media. It’s these repeated things from the people involved, and I know everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes, but I don’t believe that anymore. Not when the result is always the same: I’m kept out of the loop, I don’t have the information I need, and decisions are being made without me. It feels very deliberate, like they’re trying to push me out and then make it look like I’m the problem for noticing.

Have you ever felt that certain everyday events or the actions of others, even if they seemed minor or routine to them, were actually meant to communicate something specific to you or affect you in a particular way?

Yes, I have. I mean, I know to other people each thing sounds small. An appointment gets moved, a bill has the wrong amount, someone says they left a message, somebody doesn’t call back. Any one of those things, by itself, maybe you could explain away. I’m not saying every little inconvenience in life is aimed at me.

But this has been going on for months, and it keeps being the same kind of thing. With my sister’s appointments, somehow the information doesn’t get to me, or it gets to me too late, or someone says I should have known already. Then with the bills, they show up wrong or incomplete, and when I try to get an explanation, I’m passed around or told someone will call me back, and then they don’t. And the effect is always that I’m left without the information I need, or I’m made to look like I’m overreacting for asking basic questions.

So yes, it feels like those routine things are meant to communicate something. The message is basically, “You’re not included,” or “Stop asking,” or “We can make this difficult enough that you’ll back off.” Everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes, but I don’t believe that anymore. I worked in offices for years, I know mistakes happen, but repeated mistakes that all point in the same direction don’t feel accidental to me. They feel like a way of pushing me out of decisions and then acting like I’m the problem for noticing.

target_item.reason: The question is asking about delusional interpretations of events or others’ actions having a special meaning or being directed at the patient.

patient.answer:
Yes… though I wouldn’t put it exactly like everything strangers say is about me. It’s more that when people say certain things, or when certain things happen, they’re not as unrelated as everyone wants me to believe.

Like with my sister’s appointments—one person says, “Oh, the schedule changed,” another says, “We left a message,” and then later someone else acts surprised that I didn’t know. On the surface those are separate little comments, right? But to me they fit together. They have a meaning. They’re telling me, in a roundabout way, that I’m not supposed to be included, or that they want me to feel like I’m the one who missed something.

And the bills are the same. A bill comes in wrong, or missing information, and then when I call, someone says, “That department handles it,” or “We’ll have someone call you back,” and then nobody does. People hear that and say it’s just office confusion. But I worked in offices for years. I know what normal confusion looks like. This is different because it keeps pointing in the same direction.

So yes, I do feel that some of what people say or do has a meaning for me that other people don’t seem to see. Not like secret messages on the television or anything like that, but in the way these so-called unrelated mistakes all keep adding up to me being kept out of decisions and not given the information I should have. Everyone else calls it coincidence. I don’t think it is.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of reference or persecution that are fixed and unshakable, which would support a diagnosis of schizophrenia or a delusional disorder rather than OCD or another condition.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that events or actions by others, which seem unrelated to them, were specifically targeted at you or meant to send you a message that only you understand?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The question asks about interpreting others’ events or actions as specifically targeted or carrying a special message, which falls under the patient’s fixed delusional belief pattern.

patient.answer:
Yes, I have felt that. Not in a strange way like, you know, a coded message in the newspaper or something like that. It’s more practical than that, but it still feels very pointed.

I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved, and somehow I’m not told until after. Or someone says they called me, and I know I didn’t get a call. Then the bills show up wrong, or there’s missing information, or the details don’t match what I was told before. And when I call to sort it out, people suddenly “forget” to call me back, or they pass me around, or they act like I’m making too much of it.

If it happened once, I would let it go. I’ve worked in offices, I know mistakes happen. But when the same kind of mistake keeps happening and it always ends with me being left out or made to look like I’m the difficult one, then yes, it feels targeted. It feels like they’re sending the message that I’m not supposed to be involved, that I should just step aside and stop asking questions.

Other people keep telling me it’s just confusion or paperwork problems, but I don’t think so. I know what repeated mistakes look like, and I know when information is being kept from me. It’s the way everything adds up that people don’t seem to understand.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of reference that extend beyond the described pattern of perceived exclusion, such as believing neutral events or communications are personally directed at them.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that things you see or hear in the media, or things that strangers say or do, are meant for you or contain messages that only you understand?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The question is asking about referential or targeted beliefs—whether media or strangers’ actions contain special messages meant for the patient—which falls under delusional beliefs.

patient.answer:
No, not really with the media or strangers. I’m not sitting at home thinking the television is talking to me, or that some person in a store is sending me a secret message. That’s not what this is.

What I’m talking about is much more specific, and honestly that’s part of why it frustrates me when people try to make it sound like I’m imagining things. I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern with my sister’s situation. Her appointments get moved and somehow I’m not told, or I’m told afterward, or someone says they called when I know I didn’t get the call. Then bills show up wrong, or incomplete, or with information that doesn’t match what I was told. And then when I call to ask about it, people “forget” to call me back, or I get passed from one person to another until nobody is responsible.

So no, it’s not messages in the media. It’s these repeated things from the people involved, and I know everyone keeps saying it’s just mistakes, but I don’t believe that anymore. Not when the result is always the same: I’m kept out of the loop, I don’t have the information I need, and decisions are being made without me. It feels very deliberate, like they’re trying to push me out and then make it look like I’m the problem for noticing.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient experiences delusions of reference involving everyday events or actions by others that are perceived as having personal significance or intent.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that certain everyday events or the actions of others, even if they seemed minor or routine to them, were actually meant to communicate something specific to you or affect you in a particular way?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether everyday events or others' actions are interpreted as specifically meaningful or directed at the patient, which aligns most directly with the patient's fixed belief that repeated appointment, billing, and communication issues are deliberate attempts to keep her out of decisions.

patient.answer:
Yes, I have. I mean, I know to other people each thing sounds small. An appointment gets moved, a bill has the wrong amount, someone says they left a message, somebody doesn’t call back. Any one of those things, by itself, maybe you could explain away. I’m not saying every little inconvenience in life is aimed at me.

But this has been going on for months, and it keeps being the same kind of thing. With my sister’s appointments, somehow the information doesn’t get to me, or it gets to me too late, or someone says I should have known already. Then with the bills, they show up wrong or incomplete, and when I try to get an explanation, I’m passed around or told someone will call me back, and then they don’t. And the effect is always that I’m left without the information I need, or I’m made to look like I’m overreacting for asking basic questions.

So yes, it feels like those routine things are meant to communicate something. The message is basically, “You’re not included,” or “Stop asking,” or “We can make this difficult enough that you’ll back off.” Everyone keeps telling me it’s just mistakes, but I don’t believe that anymore. I worked in offices for years, I know mistakes happen, but repeated mistakes that all point in the same direction don’t feel accidental to me. They feel like a way of pushing me out of decisions and then acting like I’m the problem for noticing.

inference.note: The patient's responses continue to demonstrate a persistent, pattern-based belief that others are deliberately withholding information and attempting to exclude them from decision-making processes. The delusional system is non-bizarre, well-structured, and focused on a specific theme (information withholding, exclusion, and targeted mistreatment). The absence of prominent hallucinations, mood episodes, or obsessive-compulsive features rules out F20.0 (Schizophrenia) and F42.2 (Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder). The clinical picture is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Subtype 0 (F22.0), where the central theme revolves around a non-bizarre, organized belief system involving perceived deliberate mistreatment over months.
